title: resolveFinalPath infinite-loops on a recorded rename cycle (mv a b; mv b a)
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-203 finding (2026-07-25): while building the layered lineage walk, resolveFinalPath (src/reconstruction_lineage.ts) was found to follow the rename chain without a seen-set, so a transcript that records `mv a b` followed by `mv b a` — which real sessions do produce when a rename is undone — makes it loop forever rather than terminating on the cycle. The new layered walk in jfred/src/layered_lineage.ts avoids this by carrying a shared seen-set across both directions, and the engine's version was deliberately left untouched so the fix could be scoped and verified on its own. Add a seen-set (or an explicit cycle error) to resolveFinalPath and every other rename-chain walker that shares the pattern, with a unit test that records the two-hop cycle and asserts termination. No live scenario is known to trigger it yet, so a synthetic fixture is acceptable evidence.

title: renderRevisionText unconditionally appends a trailing newline, so files without one can never blob-match
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-187 finding (2026-07-25): renderRevisionText renders a revision as linesTextOf(rev).join("\n") + "\n" — the trailing newline is unconditional. A file whose real bytes do NOT end in a newline therefore can never hash-match its recorded blob. In the 68-file M sweep this produced a 2/2 correlation: exactly 2 of the 68 baseline blobs lack a trailing newline (docs/design/architecture.md ending 0x2e, docs/design/milestones.md ending 0x2e) and those are exactly the 2 baselineBlobMatched=false rows. The same artifact also corrupts the diskMatched comparison for 3 further files. Fixing this means the engine must carry a 'final line had no newline' bit, which touches the LineEntry vocabulary and every producer/consumer of it — CONFIRM the design with the user before implementing (open question 2 in plans/implementation-notes-tasks-223-224-184-203-207-187.md). Evidence: plans/166-per-file-target.md, section "Task 187 — the M-file sweep (68 files)".

title: Extend the task-224 seed clamp to the two sibling backup stampers (needs a reproducer first)
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-224 follow-up (2026-07-25): task 224 fixed the non-monotonic ladder by giving backup-sourced seeds a two-sided placement window via clampSeedBetweenPreviousAndEdit (jfred/src/reconstruction_sidecar.ts), but wired it into ONE proven site — seedStaleEditBases in jfred/src/reconstruction_reseed.ts. Two sibling stampers apply the identical `timestamp: <backupTime>` pattern and therefore share the defect CLASS: backupAfterWriteFor (reconstruction_sidecar.ts:90-96, used by reversedEditBaseSeed at reconstruction_reseed.ts:157) and backupWritesFor (reconstruction_sidecar.ts:116-122, used at reconstruction_beacons.ts:158 and via latestBackupWriteFor at reconstruction_beacons.ts:56). They were deliberately NOT changed: completeElidedBeacons and completeTruncatedBeacon are load-bearing for many character-locked scenarios (S27, S28, S30 among others) and already carry their own retiming logic — completeElidedBeacons re-times the BEACON backward when its seed precedes it — so extending the clamp without a reproducer risks breaking locked ground truths to fix a defect nobody has observed. REQUIRE a reproducing scenario that shows one of these two stampers emitting an out-of-order seed BEFORE changing them; then reuse the existing clamp and run the full suite.

title: Layer 1 View: clicking a ruler row does not jump to the first bubble with that timestamp
description: Layer 1 View bug (user report 2026-07-26, voice). In the user's words: "clicking a ruler row does not jump to the first bubble with that same time stamp." This is the task #260 feature failing in practice against the live render, despite passing its 3 unit tests. The implementation is jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-click.ts: `findBubbleForAxisPx` runs a two-stage lookup — stage 1 matches a `.filebox` whose own `--axis-px` equals the clicked tick's offset (a bubble that BEGINS at that instant), stage 2 falls back to `bubbleAxisPx + nodeAxisPx` for a bubble merely holding a node there. Re-verify against the REAL render, not the fixture: likely suspects are that the equality comparison never matches because the values are floats after task #251's content-driven spacing, or that the handler is attached to a tick element that is replaced on re-render. Note task #268 may merge duplicate ruler rows, which changes which tick is clickable.

title: Layer 1 View: merge ruler rows that display the same time value into a single row

TODAY: `formatInstantLabel` in jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts renders "MM-DD HH:MM" (no seconds, no milliseconds), and `renderRulerTicks` drops a label only when it would PHYSICALLY collide with the one above it (TICK_LABEL_MIN_GAP_PX = 13). Decide with care whether the merge happens on the DISPLAYED string or on the underlying instant, and at what precision — the user's phrasing ties it to what the label shows. Changing the number of ruler entries affects task #264 (one leader per entry) and task #266 (which tick is clickable).

title: Layer 1 View: bubble file names are truncated and should be readable

Decide the mechanism (wider or variable-width bubbles, wrapping onto a second line, a smaller font for long names, or something else) — do not simply remove the max-width, which reinstates the #245 overprinting bug.

title: Layer 1 View: global toggle to place bubbles by author vs committer timestamp
description: User request 2026-07-26, in their own wording: "add a global toggle next to the zoom buttons to place bubbles on the timeline using 'author' timestamps or committer timestamps. the 'CommitTouch' interface (/Users/matkatmusicllc/Desktop/claude code src/RevEng/jfred/src/layered_git_beacons.ts) will need 'authorEpochSeconds: number'. Line 31 'listCommitsTouchingFile' will need an optional arg (authorOrCommitter: boolean) to decide how git should be spawned (line 32) to get the author/committer timestamp." WHY THIS IS REAL, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: on 2026-07-26 the user saw two commits wrapped by task 259's same-instant rectangle whose git-GUI dates were days apart — specs/bug screenshots/'git commit timestamps computed wrong.png'. Verified against this repo: fc5ad81 and e677bd9 BOTH carry `%ct 1783459471` (2026-07-07T14:24:31-07:00) while their AUTHOR dates are Jul 4 and Jul 5. The commits were rewritten in one rebase/cherry-pick, so committer time collapsed onto one instant and author time did not. Neither reading is wrong — committer time answers 'when did this land in this repo', author time answers 'when was this change written' — so the user wants to choose per view. THE VALUE'S PATH, so the choice can be threaded end to end: (1) jfred/src/layered_git_beacons.ts:31 `listCommitsTouchingFile` is the engine's ONLY git-log reader, spawning `git log <ref> --format=%H %ct -- <path>` at line 32; (2) jfred/src/layered_instants.ts:11 `widenCommitterSecondsToInstant` turns those seconds into a Date; (3) jfred/src/layer1_commit_history.ts:29 `listPairCommitHistory` maps each touch to {hash, instant}; (4) jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts:89 `listPairNodeLadder` builds the ladder, :97 `placePairNodesOnAxis` and :112 `placeInstantOnAxis` place it; (5) jfred/src/layer1_ruler_axis.ts resolves the distinct instants into ruler rows; (6) jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts's buildPairWidget draws the bubble and jfred/webapp/layer1-tie-groups.ts groups the equal instants. TWO DESIGN NOTES FOR THE IMPLEMENTER. (a) ONE `git log --format=%H %ct %at` returns BOTH stamps in a single spawn, so if CommitTouch carries `authorEpochSeconds` AND `committerEpochSeconds`, the optional arg on listCommitsTouchingFile becomes redundant — the CALLER picks the field, and git is not re-run every time the toggle flips (the full build is ~10 s on a real project). Settle that against the arg the user described BEFORE writing either. (b) plans/coding-requirements.md forbids boolean parameters (domain types over primitives, single-condition branching), so if the arg is kept it must be a two-member enum (e.g. CommitTimeSource.author / CommitTimeSource.committer), never a boolean. UI AND PLUMBING: the toggle belongs in the header beside .zoombar in jfred/webapp/layer1.html, as its own sibling group in the style of .layerbar. The choice MUST reach the server, because the instants are computed there — the page's inputs already live in the query string (?dir=&repo=&ref=), so add a fourth param, mirror it in jfred/webapp/layer1-sources.ts's readSourceParams/fillSourceBoxesFromUrl, and read it in jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_route.ts. Flipping the toggle re-loads the view; the existing loadbar already reports that build. Finally, `widenCommitterSecondsToInstant`'s NAME and its `widenedFromSeconds` flag describe committer seconds specifically — both stamps are second-precision so the function itself is reusable, but its comment must stop claiming committer-only.

title: Layer 1 View: clicking a ruler tick must highlight the node or bubble it lands on, not just scroll to it
description: Layer 1 View feature (2026-07-26, user feedback on jfred/webapp/layer1.html). "Clicking a ruler item should scroll to the item that occurred at that ruler's timestamp, and also highlight that node or bubble." The SCROLL half already exists (task 260, jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-click.ts:79 — makeRulerTickClickable calls findBubbleForAxisPx(...)?.scrollIntoView({block:"start", inline:"center"})); what is missing is the highlight, so on a dense stage the user cannot tell WHICH bubble the tick meant. REUSE the existing highlight rather than writing a second one: jfred/webapp/layer1-find-file.ts already has landOnBubble (scrollIntoView + highlightBubble, which adds the `.found` class for HIGHLIGHT_MS = 1500 and cancels the previous bubble's un-lighting timer so two jumps in quick succession do not switch each other off). Both are module-private today — export landOnBubble and have makeRulerTickClickable call it, so the ruler tick, the typed Find box and the File Nav leaf click can never drift apart in landing behaviour. `.filebox.found` is already styled at jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css:245 (3px outline in var(--sel-edge)), so the bubble case needs no new CSS. NOTE the two-stage lookup in findBubbleForAxisPx (layer1-ruler-click.ts:64): stage 1 finds the bubble that BEGINS at that offset, stage 2 falls back to any bubble holding a NODE at it. When stage 2 is what matched, the user asked for the NODE to be highlighted rather than only its containing bubble — there is no `.node.found` rule yet, so one must be added, and findBubbleForAxisPx must return (or additionally report) the matched node so the caller knows which of the two cases fired. INTERACTS with task 284 (a ruler timestamp shared by MULTIPLE nodes), which changes what a tick click does when more than one file was touched at that instant: land the two together, or build this one as the single-match branch of 284's behaviour.

title: Layer 1 View: clicking a ruler tick shared by multiple nodes expands to list the files touched at that timestamp
description: Layer 1 View feature (2026-07-26, user feedback on jfred/webapp/layer1.html). "If multiple nodes occur at a ruler timestamp, clicking that ruler timestamp should expand and show the names of the files that were touched at that timestamp." Today a tick click is single-destination: jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-click.ts's findBubbleForAxisPx returns the FIRST match of a two-stage lookup — stage 1 the bubble that BEGINS at that offset, stage 2 any bubble holding a node at it — and makeRulerTickClickable (line 74) scrolls to it. When several files were touched at one instant that silently picks one and gives the user no way to see the others, which is the reported gap. WHAT TO BUILD: on a tick whose offset is shared by nodes in more than one bubble, the click expands an inline list of those files' paths rather than jumping. Two facts make the lookup cheap and drift-proof, both already true: a `.tick` carries the ABSOLUTE ruler offset in `--axis-px`, and a `.node`'s absolute offset is its bubble's `--axis-px` plus its own (widget-relative) one — the same arithmetic findBubbleForAxisPx already does, so collect ALL matches instead of the first. Each owning bubble's full path is on its `.fname` element's `title` attribute (its visible text is the basename only, task 245). AXIS_MATCH_EPSILON_PX (1e-6) is the tolerance to reuse — it absorbs float rounding, nothing more. OPEN CHOICES for the implementer: where the expanded list renders (inline under the tick inside the sticky `.ruler` gutter, which is only ~82px wide — `--rail-x` 80px plus the rail's 2px border — versus a popover, for which webapp/views/sidebar-coverage.ts's coverage popover and webapp/app-header.ts's toolbar popovers are the two existing patterns); whether clicking a name in that list then jumps to its bubble (probably yes); and how the list closes. INTERACTS with task 283 (a tick click must also highlight what it lands on): 283 is effectively the SINGLE-match branch of this behaviour, so land the two together or build 283 first and add this as the multi-match branch. Related but different: task 259's tie-group markers already handle two nodes of ONE bubble sharing an instant; this task is about nodes ACROSS bubbles sharing one.

description: Layer 1 View feature (2026-07-26, user feedback on jfred/webapp/layer1.html). In the user's words: "the 'git repo' text editor: when a repo is loaded, after the presence of that repo is confirmed, show a 'branch:' dropdown menu with all branch names that let the user pick the branch to use. The 'commit/branch' textbox should be replaced with a dropdown menu showing commit history. The commit dropdown menu should have a width of 75 characters (for the commit message preview) + the timestamp, so the user can see most of the commit message." TODAY: jfred/webapp/layer1.html:41-45 has `<input id="repo" type="text" size="34">` with an "Open…" picker button, and `<label>Commit / branch <input id="ref" type="text" size="10" placeholder="default branch"></label>`. Both are plain text, read by webapp/layer1-sources.ts (SOURCE_PARAM_IDS = ["dir", "repo", "ref"]) and mirrored into the URL as ?dir=&repo=&ref=, which is spec S18's "one shareable link" — so whatever the pickers become, they must still round-trip through those same query params, and fillSourceBoxesFromUrl must still be able to seed them from a link. WHAT IS NEEDED: (1) A repo-EXISTS check, which nothing does today — the current failure mode is that /api/layer1-view returns a 400 whose body message lands in the #crumb (layer1-page.ts's loadLayer1View catch). The dropdowns must appear only after the path is confirmed to be a git repo, so this needs either a new lightweight endpoint or an extension of an existing one. (2) A NEW SERVER ROUTE listing the repo's branches and its commit history — no such route exists (the page's only endpoints are /api/layer1-view, /api/pick-folder, plus /api/config and /api/projects from the classic app). The commit rows need hash, subject and committer timestamp; src/layer1_commit_history.ts and src/layered_git_beacons.ts's listCommitsTouchingFile are the existing git-log readers to model it on, and src/layered_instants.ts's widenCommitterSecondsToInstant is how committer seconds become an Instant everywhere else. (3) The branch dropdown replaces nothing — it is new UI beside the repo box. The commit dropdown REPLACES `#ref`. WIDTH: the commit dropdown is specified as 75 characters of commit-message preview plus the timestamp, so the subject must be truncated to 75 chars server- or client-side and the control sized in `ch` units, not px. OPEN QUESTIONS the implementer should settle with the user: whether picking a branch immediately reloads the view or only refills the commit list; whether the commit list is the branch's full history or a capped head window (a large repo's full log is thousands of rows in a <select>); and whether typing a raw ref must still be possible for a hash that is not in the list — the current box accepts any ref, and a dropdown alone would remove that. NOTE the ~10 s cost of /api/layer1-view (one `git log` per tracked path): the branch/commit listing must be its own fast route, never a side effect of the view build.

title: Layer 1 View: the hover-revealed full file name blends into neighbouring bubbles names
description: Layer 1 View fix (user feedback 2026-07-26, follow-up to task 280). Task 280 shipped the in-page hover reveal: `.filebox .fname:hover` in jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css lifts `max-width`/`overflow` so the whole path runs past the bubble’s 168px, painted over an opaque `background: var(--surface)` at `z-index: 7`. In the user’s words: "change the text color when showing the full file name so it doesn’t blend in with adjacent bubbles’ file names with the same y coordinate." CAUSE: the revealed name keeps `.filebox .fname`’s `color: var(--c-snap)`, the same colour every OTHER bubble’s name uses, so at one y coordinate a revealed long path reads as a single continuous run of green monospace text mixed with its neighbours’ names and the reader cannot tell where the revealed name ends. FIX DIRECTION: change the text colour (and/or raise the background contrast) inside that one `:hover` rule. The opaque background and the z-index are already in place, so this is a colour change only — no geometry change, and nothing outside `.filebox .fname:hover`. TRAP: the page is theme-aware (jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css redefines every token under `prefers-color-scheme: dark` and `[data-theme="dark"]`), so the new colour must be a token that exists in BOTH sets, not a literal.

title: Layer 1 View: dragging the File Nav resize grip causes massive GUI latency
description: Layer 1 View performance bug (user report 2026-07-26, on the task-279 feature just shipped). In the user’s words: "resizing the file nav results in massive GUI latency (probably because the entire timeline canvas is redrawn, not just the visible timeline area)". WHERE: jfred/webapp/layer1-filenav-resize.ts — every `pointermove` writes `--filenav-w` onto `.stagewrap`, and `.filenav`’s width, `.minimap`’s `left` and `.filenav-grip`’s `left` all read that property. CAUSE (to confirm): `.filenav` is a flex SIBLING of `main.timelines` inside `.stagewrap`, so changing its width reflows the timeline pane — and that pane holds ~800 `.filebox` widgets spanning ~156,000px inside a `zoom`-scaled `.canvas`, so each pointermove forces a layout of the WHOLE canvas rather than the visible area. Candidate fixes to weigh: (a) coalesce the writes to one per frame with requestAnimationFrame, the smallest change; (b) take the timeline pane out of the resize’s layout path so its width is not a function of the pane’s — e.g. a fixed flex-basis on `main.timelines`, or drive the pane’s offset instead of the flex row; (c) commit the width only on `pointerup` and show a lightweight preview line during the drag. Verify the cause before picking — if (a) alone makes it smooth, (b) and (c) are unnecessary. Related: task 192 covers this page’s other bounded-perf work.

title: Layer 1 View: the dashed leader lines and ruler tick labels sit ~52 px above the nodes they mark
description:
Layer 1 View alignment bug, found independently by two agents on 2026-07-26 while working tasks 270 and 268/275/266, and deliberately NOT fixed then: it moves the vertical alignment of every row on the canvas, which the user should sign off on rather than have changed as a side effect of other work.

MECHANISM. A `.filebox` is positioned by `margin-top: calc(var(--axis-px) * 1px)` (jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css), so its BORDER-BOX top is the bubble's first instant. Its nodes live in `.lane`, the first in-flow child, which starts after the bubble's 2 px border and its 50 px `padding-top`. A node's absolute canvas y is therefore `axisPx + 52`, while `.leader` (`top: calc(var(--axis-px) * 1px)`, positioned against `.canvas`) and `.ruler .tick` (same, against `.ruler`) are both drawn at bare `axisPx`. So the dashed connector and the gutter timestamp both sit ~52 px above the dots they are meant to mark.

The comment on `.leaders` claims task 265 made the line land on the nodes — "a node is placed at axisPx - startPx inside a bubble whose own offset is startPx, so its absolute canvas y is exactly axisPx" — but that derivation omits the border and the header padding, so task 265 did not achieve what it documents. Fix the comment along with the geometry.

The 52 px is not a constant of nature: it is `.filebox`'s border plus its `padding-top`, and that padding is itself DERIVED from `.fname`/`.sub`'s `top` values and font sizes (see the derivation comment on `.filebox`), so any change to the bubble header moves it. Task 270 briefly made it 70 px before being reverted.

DECIDE THE FIX WITH CARE: adding the header offset to BOTH `.leader` and `.ruler .tick` keeps the gutter, the dashed lines and the dots agreeing with each other; moving only one of the two would make the ruler disagree with the leaders. Publishing the offset once as a custom property beats repeating the literal in two rules.

VERIFY AGAINST THE REAL RENDER BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING. This is a reasoned reading of the CSS, not a measured screenshot, and the current alignment has shipped through tasks 250, 262, 264 and 265 without complaint — so confirm the offset is really visible before moving every line on the page.
